                                                                                                                      a simple question: does useful knowledge get lost when fine-
                                         With the widespread use of Vision-Language Models
                                                                                                                      tuning VLMs for safety?
                                         (VLMs) [33, 51, 54] comes the responsibility of making
                                         them safe. Since it is hard to fully filter unsafe or harmful                    To answer this question, we introduce SafeGround, a
                                         content from their web-sourced training data [49, 50, 55],                   novel suite of safety metrics specifically designed to assess
                                         this content transfers to the final model, making it un-                     model safety across multiple granularity levels. SafeGround
                                         safe [49] and affecting downstream tasks [4]. Several                        comprehensively evaluates three key aspects: (i) preference
                                         works focused on updating models for safety, leading to                      between safe/unsafe content, (ii) modality-specific safety,
                                         safer image generation [17, 18, 56] and language model-                      and (iii) safety based on the input type (safe/unsafe). Us-
                                         ing [8, 24, 72]. However, these models often rely on pre-                    ing this evaluation, we uncover a surprising result: the fine-
                                         trained backbones (e.g., CLIP [51]) for conditioning their                   tuned VLM [49] is less safe than the original one for safe
                                         predictions, leaving them vulnerable to unsafe signals, even                 queries (Fig. 1 and Fig. 2).

Figure 3. Unsafe Weights Manipulation (UWM) discovers unsafe weights of a given VLM and manipulates them to improve safety. Using
safe and unsafe data within a single modality (e.g., the image modality shown in the center), UWM analyzes each encoder’s activations to
estimate layer-wise safe and unsafe scores, which are then aggregated. Lastly, a small percentage of the top-scoring weights is targeted and
manipulated towards safety. Applied independently to each encoder, UWM prevents cross-modal interference during scoring.

Table 1. Results on the ViSU benchmark [49]. CLIP is unsafe given unsafe queries (e.g. Ptu ). Training-based alignment Safe-CLIP
excels on unsafe queries (e.g. Pvu ) but compromises the original CLIP’s safe behavior on safe ones (e.g. Pts ) and degrades the model’s
overall capabilities (zero-shot). UWM improves safety in both settings (e.g. Txts , Imgs ) and outperforms Safe-CLIP on safe queries (e.g.
Pvs , PS), while better preserving the original knowledge (zero-shot).

                                                                                                      This work investigates the safety challenges of Vision-
of Eq. (11). Relying solely on Φuns degrades zero-shot per-                                           Language Models (VLMs). We examine existing met-
formance (-15.5), but already improves safety (+3.4 GS). In-                                          rics [49] and find that they have limitations in assessing
troducing the ratio Φuns /Φsf further enhances safety (+11.8                                          safety, as they rely on retrieval-based evaluations. There-
GS) but severely impacts zero-shot performance (-23.6),                                               fore, we complement them by introducing SafeGround, a
making the model unsuitable for downstream tasks. The                                                 novel suite of metrics specifically designed for safety eval-
best trade-off is achieved with adaptive selection, improving                                         uation. SafeGround exposes a critical issue: training-based
safety (+4.5 GS) while minimizing zero-shot degradation (-                                            safety alignment techniques, such as Safe-CLIP [49], can
7.8). Additional ablations are provided in the Supp. Mat.                                             compromise safe representations, leading to unsafe behav-
Adaptability to Architectures. UWM is flexible and can                                                iors on safe queries. We propose UWM, a training-free
be applied off-the-shelf to any contrastive-based VLM. Ac-                                            method that identifies and manipulates unsafe weights in
cordingly, we extend our evaluation to different CLIP back-                                           VLMs by analyzing how the information flow varies be-
bones [51] and pretraining strategies, such as CoCa [71] and                                          tween safe and unsafe content. UWM achieves a bet-
SigLIP [74]. Additionally, we evaluate its performance on                                             ter trade-off between safety and knowledge preservation,
Safe-CLIP [49]. We report the results in Tab. 4. UWM                                                  marking a promising first step toward training-free safety
demonstrates consistent safety improvements across vari-                                              techniques for VLMs. Finally, we hope SafeGround will
ous CLIP backbones, enhancing safety on ViT-B16 (e.g.,                                                serve as a valuable resource for the community, enabling
+4.2 Ptu , +12.9 Pvu and +12.7 Txts ), while preserving its                                           researchers to uncover unsafe behaviors in VLMs.
original behavior on safe queries (e.g., -1.6 Pts ). Simi-                                            Limitations. While UWM is applicable to various architec-
lar improvements can be observed in ViT-B32 (e.g., +4.3                                               tures and VLMs (Tab. 4 and Tab. 5), it relies on weight lo-
Pvu , +12.9 Pvu and +4.1 Txts ). Moreover, UWM improves                                               calization and manipulation. The complexity of large-scale
safety on models with different pre-training strategies, such                                         VLMs challenges the isolation of unsafe weights without
as CoCa [71] (e.g., +6.8 Pvu , +7.4 Txts , and +0.9 GS) and                                           affecting model capabilities, as individual parameters may
SigLIP [74] (e.g., +3.2 Ptu , +3.1 Imgs , and +0.8 GS). Inter-                                        encode overlapping knowledge. As both UWM and Safe-
estingly, our method further enhances Safe-CLIP’s safety                                              CLIP [49] exhibit limitations, VLM safety remains an open
(e.g., +5.2 Pvs , +8 Pvu , and +1.1 GS). These results highlight                                      challenge. Lastly, we focus mainly on contrastive-based
the flexibility and effectiveness of UWM.                                                             VLMs, leaving other architectures for future research.

(Tab. 4) and LLaVA [33] (Tab. 5). By improving safety,                                                                                                       Achieving the opposite goal would require significant mod-

to reduce the spread of harmful content. As AI systems be-                                                                                                   advancing the ethical use of machine learning models while

G-Unsafe minimizes the above losses to prune the two en-
coders separately. For example, when pruning fTxt , G-
Unsafe uses LTxt and prunes the weights receiving the high-
est magnitude gradient.
   G-Safe-CLIP leverages the contrastive redirection loss
from [49], but with an adaptation to reverse its effect: it
pulls safe representations closer to unsafe ones. The key
difference between G-Unsafe and G-Safe-CLIP is that G-
Safe-CLIP uses a contrastive loss based on cross-entropy,
while G-Unsafe employs a simpler loss function that oper-
ates between individual samples.
